notes:
Lead background:
- SMB ecommerce checkout & support platform. Founded 2020, Series A, building conversational upsell + ticket deflection.

Initial discovery summary:
- First intro call 2026-03-02 (FF id ff_2026-03-02_4982). AE Riley intro; SE Priya joined.
- They signed up for self-serve trial (public cloud) and ran a small sandbox integration.
- Observed bursts during morning flash sale test (9:00-9:15 PST) that triggered repeated 429s from their current provider. Quote from CTO: "We saw 30% of requests hit 429 in the first 10 minutes — unacceptable for checkout flows."

Workload and traffic profile:
- Primary workloads: chat-driven checkout suggestions + short support dialogs + automated order emails.
- Expected steady baseline: ~15 req/s during business hours. Spikes: up to 250 req/s for 5-15 minutes during promos.
- Typical request payloads small (prompt + metadata), average response tokens ~60. Latency target: p95 < 400ms for UI flows. Cost sensitivity: high — looking to keep monthly cloud inference spend under $2k initially.

Technical requirements & acceptance criteria:
- Must avoid hard 429s during short bursts; need burst handling strategy, retry guidance, and shadowing for canary.
- Concurrency and per-second quotas: want clear default quotas + ability to request temporary burst credits for scheduled promos.
- Prefer public cloud hosted API (no VPC/private yet).
- Audit logs required for support/debug (audit_logging).
- Minimal integration effort; prefer SDK examples and a short test harness.

Questions from SE/Engineering:
- What are Redwood Hosted default rate limits (requests/sec, concurrent streams)? How are 429s surfaced (Retry-After header)?
- Are there automatic short-term burst allowances or queueing? Can Redwood temporarily raise limit for scheduled events?
- Does Redwood expose token vs request metrics at token-level for cost analysis?

Recent activity timeline:
- 2026-03-02: Discovery call, demo of hosted API endpoints, shared test plan.
- 2026-03-03: Sent pricing deck and quickstart link (drive/redwood-pricing-deck-influxguard_v1.pdf).
- 2026-03-05: Customer onboarded SDK; ran first promo simulation, observed 429s with current provider. Asked Redwood for PoC.
- 2026-03-09: Internal sync w/ SE to scope 1-week spike PoC.
- 2026-03-10: AE to provision trial credits and coordinate PoC kick-off; customer awaiting SE schedule.

PoC proposal (SE recommended):
- 7-day spike PoC on Redwood Hosted API in us-east-1. Baseline 50 req/s, controlled bursts 200-300 req/s for 10min windows.
- Use Redwood rate-limit headers and Retry-After best-practices (exponential backoff + jitter).
- Monitor p95 latency, 429 counts, token usage; Redwood to provide temporary burst allowance or documented fallback plan.

Next steps / owner actions:
- AE (Riley): provision trial credits and send calendar invite for PoC kickoff (actioned).
- SE (Priya): deliver PoC test script, define pass/fail (max allowable 429 % < 2% during bursts), instrument metrics dashboards.
- Customer (CTO / Eng lead): confirm promo schedule and internal budget gating.

Open blockers / risks:
- Customer requires concrete assurances around short-term burst handling (they prefer not to build complex client-side retry logic initially).
- Budget approval timeline unclear — may delay converting after PoC even if successful.
